slides.title: Exit code, hang and timeout
slides.source: Source: Chapter 0, “The headless test”; glossary, Toolchain.
slides.notes: Run lengths are illustrative; the 30 s limit is an example.
slides.picture: Three runs on a time axis: one finishes with exit code 0, one finishes with code 1, one hangs until a 30 second timeout stops it.

new_texts: A number a program returns; 0 means success.
finishes, and says it went wrong
Every finished run returns a number. 0 means success; anything else means something went wrong.
all_texts: A number a program returns; 0 means success.
finishes, and says it went wrong
Every finished run returns a number. 0 means success; anything else means something went wrong.

new_texts: A hang is a run that never finishes. It returns no number, so a script waiting for one waits for ever.
all_texts: A number a program returns; 0 means success.
finishes, and says it went wrong
A hang is a run that never finishes. It returns no number, so a script waiting for one waits for ever.

new_texts: A limit after which a run is stopped.
stopped at 30 s: counts as a failure
A timeout stops it at a set time. Treat the stop as a failure, not as success.
all_texts: A number a program returns; 0 means success.

new_texts: Convert a source file into the form the engine uses.
convert a source file for the engine
a stored result, maybe out of date
Imported once: the copy matches the source.

new_texts: A question asking you to approve an action.
At first every action asks. Safe, but you click six times, and tired people click yes.

slides.notes: The speed 160.0 to 192.0 test and its 2 failures are from Chapter 1.
slides.picture: A list of project rules the agent reads first. Then two instructions, one vague and one checkable, each run against a test.

new_texts: A standing file of project rules the agent reads, such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.
a check can pass or fail
- Run Godot with --headless, never with a window.
- Pin the time step with --fixed-fps 60 in tests.
- Do not change tuning.gd without asking.
- Report the exit code of every run.
The instruction file holds standing rules, so you do not repeat them. Keep them short and checkable.

slides.title: Frames are not seconds
slides.source: Source: Chapter 0, “The time trap”; Chapter 1; glossary, Toolchain.
slides.notes: 22.4 s and 0.34 s are from Chapter 1 and the Chapter 0 headless run.
slides.picture: Two balls moving at 30 and 144 frames a second. With delta both go the same distance in a second. Then a real-time test run against one with a fixed frame rate.

new_texts: The simulation's clock, as opposed to the wall clock.
Without delta the 144 fps ball would go 4.8 times as far.
Motion is measured in seconds, not frames. Using delta keeps a ball's speed the same at any frame rate.
all_texts: The simulation's clock, as opposed to the wall clock.
Without delta the 144 fps ball would go 4.8 times as far.
Motion is measured in seconds, not frames. Using delta keeps a ball's speed the same at any frame rate.

new_texts: Rendering locked to a set number of frames a second so runs match.
A constant step length forced on the simulation.
TIME TO RUN THE SAME 25-CHECK TEST (SECONDS)
About 66 times faster, with identical results.
A fixed frame rate pins the time step. The test then runs the same way every time, and in a third of a second.
